articles.headline: Chris Pratt Officially Confirms Star-Lord's Return to the MCU
keyFacts: Chris Pratt confirmed that Star-Lord will return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe in a future project.
Pratt stated that Marvel Studios has taken hard action to fulfill the promise of the character's return.
The actor did not disclose a specific timeline or project for when Star-Lord will reappear.
body: We haven't seen Chris Pratt's Star-Lord in the Marvel Cinematic Universe since 2023, when James Gunn's Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy definitively concluded. Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 ended on a hard reset for Star-Lord (aka Peter Quill), with the intergalactic hero returning to Earth and finding new purpose: enjoying Terran cereal and contemplating an amateur career in landscaping.

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 promised that "The legendary Star-Lord will return." Years later, Pratt says this will happen, and that 'hard action' has been taken to bring back at least one of the Guardians.
The future of Guardians of the Galaxy in the MCU

In an interview on The Playlist's Bingeworthy podcast, Pratt expanded on comments from earlier this year about Star-Lord's promised return to the MCU. "I have a great relationship with Kevin [Feige] and Lou [D’Esposito]," Pratt said, "and there have been both ongoing conversations about how we make good on that promise and also hard action taken to make sure that we make good on that promise. So yeah, you’ll see Star-Lord again, which is very exciting, but I’m not at liberty to say when that’s going to be, but he’s not going anywhere."

In a previous podcast appearance, Pratt said that he has an idea of how Marvel Studios will use him in a future project, but he wasn't at liberty to say if he'd return in either of the next two Avengers movies: Doomsday and Secret Wars. Asked by Happy Sad Confused podcast host Josh Horowitz whether he would potentially return to lead a new Guardians team without Gunn at the helm, Pratt was non-committal.

"Everything is all liquid, right?" he said at the time. "They kind of take things a step at a time at Marvel. I'm happy to do anything they want me to do — and will. Also, I personally have a really strong vision of what I would want [Star-Lord] to do, and I think it's [fucking] great. I'm down to contribute any way I can to them setting up the next 10 years of storytelling and I have a pretty strong idea of how I can contribute to that."

Pratt first appeared as Star-Lord in 2014's Guardians of the Galaxy and reprised the role in two direct sequels and the Disney Plus special presentation The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special. He also guest-starred in Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame, and made a cameo appearance in Thor: Love and Thunder.

While Star-Lord is currently back on Earth, the multiversal shenanigans promised in Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars mean pretty much anything can happen. Much of the Doomsday cast has been officially revealed, but directors Joe and Anthony Russo have teased surprise reveals still to come.

Pratt's character could also reasonably return in the recently announced Nova movie, which will reportedly feature the Richard Rider version of the character. Star-Lord ended up being quite friendly with the Nova Corps in the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise; a buddy space-cop movie with Pratt, John C. Reilly's Rhomann Dey, and Richard Rider sounds like a potentially great time.
Pratt's latest project, season 2 of the Prime Video series The Terminal List, debuted earlier this week.

articles.headline: Trump pushback, Biden 'disaster' and gender surprise: 5 key moments from Kansas Senate debate
keyFacts: Republican Senator Roger Marshall and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton debated in Kansas as both parties compete for U.S. Senate control.
Both candidates addressed personal controversies involving unpaid medical bills and handling church camp abuse allegations.
Hamilton called Biden's border policies a disaster, while Marshall noted he does not always agree with President Trump.
body: Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton sparred over President Donald Trump, immigration, Iran, transgender athletes, artificial intelligence and personal controversies during a contentious Kansas Senate debate Wednesday night.

The hourlong showdown came less than two weeks before Election Day as Marshall seeks a second term and Hamilton, a longtime pastor, tries to become the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate from Kansas since 1932.

The race has drawn increased national attention as Republicans and Democrats battle for control of the Senate, with Trump traveling to Kansas earlier this week to campaign for Marshall — a topic touched on during the debate.
Here are five moments that stood out from Wednesday night's debate.
SLEEPER SENATE RACE EMERGES AS UNEXPECTED HEADACHE FOR REPUBLICANS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS
The debate wasted little time getting contentious, opening with questions about controversies that have fueled attacks against both candidates.
Marshall was confronted with a New York Times review that found his former medical practice sued more than 700 patients over unpaid bills.
"Every year we gave away $3 to $4 million of charity, but we also had a business," Marshall responded. "We had 300 employees, we had a mortgage payment, we had electric."
Hamilton, meanwhile, was questioned about his handling of allegations involving a volunteer at his church's summer camp who was accused of sexual abuse.
Hamilton acknowledged that he should have ensured the individual did not return to the camp following an initial investigation.
FROM 'THIRD REICH' TO ‘NOT THAT INFORMED’: SENATE DEBATES DELIVER FIREWORKS BEFORE MIDTERMS
"I should have checked to make sure that he wasn't going back," Hamilton said. "That was a mistake on my part."
Trump became part of the debate after moderators played footage from the president's campaign appearance for Marshall in Kansas earlier in the week.
"And at this election, I'm asking you to pretend, please, that I'm on the ballot. Just pretend," Trump told the crowd.
Marshall was then asked whether Trump's support meant Kansans should expect him to back every part of the president's agenda.
"No," Marshall responded, saying there had been "multiple times" when he objected to Trump.
Pressed to identify a specific disagreement, Marshall pointed to recent immigration enforcement in southwest Kansas and Trump's approach to beef imports .
"Just like with my wife, I can disagree with her. My wife is always right," Marshall joked. "And President Trump is not always right."
Marshall nevertheless urged Trump voters to turn out for him, arguing that electing Hamilton could help Democrats capture the Senate.
The two rivals found themselves in agreement when the moderator asked each candidate how many genders there are.
"There's two. There's a boy and there's a girl," Marshall said. "I delivered 5,000 of them and almost half were boys and half were girls."
"There are two genders, male and female ," Hamilton responded.
TOP TAKEAWAYS FROM JD VANCE TOWN HALL: COSTLY GAS, DC CORRUPTION, IMMIGRATION HOT TAKES AND THE WAR
The candidates then turned to the debate over transgender participation in women's sports .
Hamilton said decisions over athletic eligibility should generally be made locally but was unequivocal about whether biological males should compete against females.
"I have a 12-year-old granddaughter. I don't want biological men or boys competing against her that could harm her," Hamilton said. "It's not a fair, fair fight."
Marshall argued that by high school, "boys need to be in boys sports, girls in girls sports," while accusing national Democrats of pushing "transgender ideology."
Hamilton later accused Marshall of using the issue to "pick on" and "bully" people.
Hamilton called for greater federal oversight of artificial intelligence and compared the emerging technology to the development of nuclear power and nuclear weapons.
"We developed a Nuclear Regulatory Commission. We need to do the same thing with AI," Hamilton said.
But when the moderator pressed him to identify specific federal regulations he would support, Hamilton acknowledged he did not yet have an answer.
"You know what? I'm not sure, to be honest," Hamilton said, arguing that even experts are struggling to understand the technology's potential dangers.

Marshall advocated a "light touch" approach focused on national security, transparency, protecting children and privacy, while slamming a one-size-fits-all global order for artificial intelligence advancement.
Hamilton pushed back sharply.
"This is an existential — potential existential threat to the human race," Hamilton said. "We can't just go with a light touch and hope everybody does their best."
BIDEN CONSPICUOUSLY ABSENT FROM CAMPAIGN TRAIL AS OBAMA, HARRIS STEP UP FOR MIDTERM PUSH
Hamilton sought to put distance between himself and former President Joe Biden when moderators challenged the Democrat over his claim that he would "lead from the middle."

The moderator pointed to Hamilton's past donations to Democrats, including Biden, former Vice President Kamala Harris and Rep. Sharice Davids, D-Kan., before asking him to identify a progressive policy he opposed.
"The Biden policies when it came to the border were a disaster," Hamilton responded. "I believe in strong and secure borders."
"I'm not somebody who favors the Socialist Party," Hamilton added. "I'm somebody who stands in the middle."
Hamilton also reiterated during the debate that he would not support Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer for majority leader if Democrats capture control of the chamber.

articles.headline: ESPN analysts believe J.J. McCarthy could lead Giants to playoffs

ESPN analysts Andrew Hawkins and Adam Schefter suggested that McCarthy could lead the Giants to a division title and playoff contention.
McCarthy is scheduled to make his first start for the Giants against the Houston Texans this Sunday.
body: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) and New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) during a week 6 NFL football game between New York Giants and New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. After a season-ending injury to starter Jaxson Dart, the New York Giants have been forced into taking a fluid approach to their starting quarterback situation and are now turning to their third starter of the year. Just over three weeks after trading for J.J. McCarthy, New York is officially moving him to starter and benching Jameis Winston, who relieved Dart.
On Thursday’s episode of Get Up, Andrew Hawkins and Adam Schefter discussed what the move could mean not just for the Giants but for the rest of the NFC East as well.

“There’s no one who is sticking out in this division, no one who’s playing well,” Hawkins said. “When you look at even the quarterback play throughout the division, I remember when Harbaugh first came, and there was so much excitement around what he could bring to this organization and Jackson Dart and everything he can bring out of him.”
“If [J.J. McCarthy] plays the way he did in the 4th [quarter], [the Giants are] the favorites in the division.”

Hawkins went on to say that McCarthy producing could make the Giants the favorites in the division, which would put New York back in the playoffs.

“The conversation was still, well, he’s the fourth-best quarterback in the division. Well, now that we’re this part in the season, no quarterback has really stood out, right? The Giants had their issues and concern, but I would say everything around the quarterback position, obviously, because Jaxson Dart has been out for the New York Giants, has actually looked up a lot quicker than we expected from (tight end Isaiah Likely) of the world.

“Nabers looks like a top 10 wide receiver the way we expected before injury. So if you can get a little bit outta J.J., really, they’re in contention. And not only that, they’re probably, for my money, if he plays the way he did in the fourth, the favorites in the division.”
Schefter pointed back to how high McCarthy was drafted as a potential indicator of what he’s capable of.

“Look, if Jaxson Dart were healthy this year, they would be the favorites to win the division,” he said. “They’re now getting a quarterback who at one point was the 10th overall pick in a draft in where Caleb Williams went one, Jayden Daniels went two, and Drake Maye went three. They believe he’s got that type of ability. If they can harness that type of ability, which the Vikings were willing to just give up on it, and they have a chance to win the division and set up the franchise.”
McCarthy’s first start for New York will come on Sunday against the Houston Texans.

body: Thuram deal, 3️⃣ Milan names, Roma-Bakola, ADL won't sell: today's news 🔥 The three days of European action wrap up today with Europa League and Conference League fixtures. Juventus, Milan and Atalanta are the Italian sides in action, facing Rennes, Bournemouth and Ajax respectively.
Between those matches, transfer news and injury updates, there is plenty to talk about today.

As usual, here are the biggest stories.
🤑 Juventus, Bremer to leave? Yes, but...

Juventus could consider selling Gleison Bremer as early as January. According to Calciomercato.com , the Brazilian defender has reportedly attracted interest from Bayer Leverkusen , who are ready to explore a move to bring him to Germany during the winter transfer window. The centre-back, born in 1997, recently sparked controversy with comments about some teammates’ lack of character following the defeat to Lazio, an issue that was subsequently resolved with an apology to Luciano Spalletti .

Juventus do not consider Bremer untouchable, but his departure would depend on a particularly high offer. The defender is a key member of the squad, earning around €6 million per season . Any move therefore hinges on Bayer’s willingness to meet Juventus’ financial demands, as the club have no intention of easily letting go of one of their most important players.
🤩 Milan dream of Scott, with two more midfield targets

Milan are exploring potential moves to strengthen their midfield, assessing targets for January or next summer. Top of the list is Alex Scott , the Bournemouth midfielder who has impressed in the Premier League and is also being tracked by several leading English clubs. However, Milan will not be able to use today’s match to watch the player, born in 2003, up close, as he is injured. A deal would be difficult regardless, with the Cherries hoping to sell their star for a fee close to €100 million.

According to TMW , the other two targets would be easier to land: Yasin Ayari of Brighton and Adem Zorgane of Union Saint-Gilloise. The former can play both as a holding midfielder and an attacking midfielder, and his contract expires in 2027, a detail that could influence the English club’s valuation. Milan are monitoring the various situations without having settled on a definitive strategy: opportunities over the coming months will determine which targets they pursue.
✍️ Inter begin talks over Thuram contract extension

Inter are stepping up efforts to secure Marcus Thuram ’s long-term future. The French striker’s contract expires in 2028, but both sides want to begin talks now over an extension. According to TMW , initial contacts have been positive, paving the way for formal negotiations.

The aim is to agree a deal running until 2030 , strengthening the bond between Inter and one of their key attacking players. Talks will continue over the coming weeks, with both sides keen to reach an agreement quickly. Their shared desire to continue together is an important first step towards a new deal.
🙅‍♂️ Napoli, ADL: "I’m not selling! I turned down €3.5 billion"

Aurelio De Laurentiis has dismissed rumours of a possible sale of Napoli to American businessman Matt Rizzetta . Speaking to Radio Kiss Kiss , the Napoli president ruled out any intention of selling the club: " Napoli is not for sale. I have no intention of proceeding ." De Laurentiis also explained that, if he ever decided to sell, he would prefer to hand the club over to a Neapolitan businessman rather than an American.

The owner also reiterated his determination to press ahead with plans to build a new stadium, stressing that he had already rejected huge offers in the past. " Years ago, I turned down €3.5 billion from Arab buyers ," he said. As for Rizzetta, De Laurentiis confirmed that he had received an approach about a potential sale, but had replied that there was no intention of selling Napoli.
🔜 Roma: Bakola a target, but not for January

Roma are keeping a close eye on Bakola , Sassuolo’s young French midfielder, who has also attracted interest from Juventus and several Premier League clubs. According to TMW , however, Sassuolo have no intention of letting him go during the winter transfer window. Having arrived from Marseille last February for close to €10 million, the French youngster has already made eight appearances across Serie A and the Coppa Italia, catching the eye of several clubs with his ability.

Sassuolo see Bakola as an important player for the second half of the season and aim to keep him until at least June as they look to secure comfortable survival under Alberto Aquilani . A January move therefore looks difficult for Roma: Sassuolo’s management appear unwilling to enter negotiations during this transfer window and would prefer to postpone any decisions on the midfielder’s future until the summer.
🤕 Lazio, Gud’s return delayed!

Albert Gudmundsson will have to wait a little longer before returning to action. According to Il Messaggero , the latest examinations showed that the bone callus in his right shoulder has not yet fully formed. The forward will therefore miss the first matches of November and is targeting a return after the international break.

Ahead of the match against Parma, Marusic and Rovella remain unavailable, while Cancellieri is ready to return to the squad. Cataldi is also nearing a return and could rotate with Belahyane to manage workloads in midfield.
😔 Fiorentina, Antognoni regrets missing centenary celebrations

Giancarlo Antognoni has reflected on his decision not to attend Fiorentina ’s centenary celebrations, organised by the Commisso family. " I do feel some regret about not going, for the fans, not for the owners ," he told Torpedone , the Autolinee Toscane podcast, explaining that past disagreements had influenced his decision. The former Fiorentina icon nevertheless stressed that he had never had any problems with Joseph Commisso or Rocco’s wife, Catherine.

Antognoni also commented on the team’s current situation, calling for the squad to be given time following a turnover of 13 players. " You can’t have everything straight away with such sweeping changes," he stressed, expressing confidence in Paolo Vanoli ’s work.

articles.headline: The Switch 2 Has Been Jailbroken For The First Time
keyFacts: The Nintendo Switch 2 has been jailbroken for the first time using an exploit co-created with AI.
The hack allows users to mod games and install homebrew by running a specific backward-compatible game during startup.
Nintendo is expected to address the vulnerability by removing the identified game from the e-store or updating console firmware.
body: The ongoing fallout from yesterday’s PHP vulnerability and patching continues to dominate headlines, with AI credited for both discovering the serious 20-year-old flaw, and for exploiting it in the moments after the patch was released. Now, word is out that the Nintendo Switch 2 has been jailbroken just 16 months after its original launch, again thanks to AI.

WCCF Tech reports that the new exploit is based on a discovery made back in July, a so-called “userland exploit,” which allowed external code to be run within a specific app or game. That was a significant dent in Nintendo’s defenses, but not yet a way to allow piracy. However, this latest discovery takes things a stage further, with an in-software hack now allowing users to mod games, install homebrew (and therefore potentially pirated games), and download save files. Centro Leaks reposted a video clip from someone claiming to be a jailbreaker in which they show characters like Peter Griffin and Hatsune Miku modded into Mario Kart World.
BREAKING: SWITCH 2 HAS BEEN HACKED (BY AI!), FIRST JAILBREAK RELEASED https://t.co/DzTLzai44g
— Centro LEAKS (@CentroLeaks) October 22, 2026

The individual responsible claims to have used OpenAI Codex to co-create the hack, and says it took “substantial effort” for around two weeks to achieve, using a setup that looks like a Rube Goldberg device. The method requires running a specific backward-compatible Switch 1 game in order to take advantage of the previous exploit, and this needs to be done every time the Switch 2 is launched. Which is to say, it’s still a ways off from being a commonplace way in which people will jailbreak their Switches for piracy. The person responsible has also publicly identified the e-store game which is being used, says WCCFT, so Nintendo can remove it fairly easily.

These attempts are always portrayed as being a means to run “homebrew” games on closed systems, and while there are undeniably large homebrew communities out there who want to create and play games on the Switch 2, it’s always far more motivated by piracy. If you can install a homemade game, you can also install a ROM of an official release.

The initial version of the Switch 1 was also pretty quickly cracked, but in that case via hardware and in such a way that Nintendo couldn’t patch out. That was a far more serious vulnerability for Nintendo, which could only repair the issue in further manufacturing of the console, leaving those launch versions of the Switch 1 still able to be jailbroken today. And Nintendo came down on those selling pre-jailbroken SwitchesÂ hard. This isn’t that, but it is the first big crack in the armor and will inevitably be further explored, and that’s a process that’s far easier today thanks to the willingness of AI models to merrily poke at the code looking for weaknesses far faster than humans ever could.

It’s worth noting that the Switch 2’s backward compatibility was taken advantage of almost immediately after the release of the Switch 2, when Switch 1 ROM carts were quickly adapted to run older games on the new device, but Nintendo was able to detect this use and ban the users from their own devices. This latest trick is said to be able to evade Nintendo’s online checks.

We’re still a ways off from custom firmware, given the current exploit is “tethered” (the modification isn’t permanent, and has to be performed every time), but Nintendo will certainly already be exploring ways to update its own firmware in ways that could combat the techniques. We’ve reached out to Nintendo to ask for comment.

articles.headline: Ilhan Omar says 'bizarre' pre-dawn raid on her home is forcing her to leave
keyFacts: Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar stated she is leaving her Washington DC home because safety concerns following a federal raid make living there unfeasible.
Homeland Security Investigations agents searched her home on October 12, seizing 17 items including phones and notebooks as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
The government has not specified what crime Omar is accused of, while subpoenas have also been issued to members of her family.
body: - Published
Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar has said she can no longer live in her Washington DC home after it was searched by federal agents last week, fearing her address has been exposed after the raid.
"With the death threats that I deal with, it's not, it's no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids," she told MSN NOW, external.

In Omar's first public interview since the pre-dawn search of her home, she detailed how Homeland Security Investigations agents seized over a dozen items, including cell phones and notebooks, as part of an investigation.
The government has not said what crime Omar is accused of but that the raid was "part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation".
The search follows multiple comments from officials that cast doubt on Omar's US citizenship, which she received in 2000 after her arrival from Kenya.

More than a dozen subpoenas have also been issued to members of Omar's family, as part of the investigation, and it was reported that her personal computers and passport were among the items that were seized.
Recalling the hourslong raid of her home with MS NOW, Omar said: "It obviously did freak all of us out."
Omar said agents began "pounding on the doors" of her home at around 06:00 EDT (11:00 BST) on 12 October, startling her and her husband, who were both in bed.
"We were screaming," she said, as the couple ran downstairs to see what was happening, calling the incident "so bizarre".
The Minnesota Democrat estimated that between15 to 25 agents encircled her home, all of whom she said "conducted themselves in a decent way".
Agents presented Omar with a warrant at the door after she asked for one.

She then watched from the couch as agents spent roughly five hours going from room to room, Omar said, leaving with a total of 17 items, including multiple cellphones, notebooks, and her husband's camera from the 1960s.
The BBC contacted the Justice Department for comment after being referred by the DHS.
Omar again criticised the government's investigation, suggesting that it was meant to be intimidating.
Immediately following the raid last week, she posted a statement online where she called it "an outrageous abuse of power" and "weaponisation of federal law enforcement to target political enemies".
Former President Barack Obama has also blasted the federal probe, saying in a lengthy statement that it was "so appalling".
Omar, who has represented Minnesota since 2018, has long been a target of President Donald Trump's, who has repeatedly suggested she "go back" to Somalia.
He has denied any involvement in her investigation, saying it has "nothing to do with me".
At an Ohio rally in October, Trump referred to the search of her home, saying: "I don't know what they're doing with it, but I can tell you this: she's a disaster."
The congresswoman, however, rejected the president's response, arguing that "he's got everything to do with it".
"You know, this goes back to 2019 when he was screaming about the fact that, you know, I, I need to be sent back, I need to be deported."

articles.headline: How much money does Gianni Infantino make? FIFA responds to retracted report over compensation
keyFacts: The Times retracted a report claiming FIFA president Gianni Infantino received an undisclosed second salary.
FIFA stated that payments from the 2026 World Cup entity were reimbursements and expenses, not compensation, under Swiss law.
FIFA accepted an apology from The Times and warned of ongoing efforts to undermine the organization and its leadership.
body: Editor's note: This story was originally published on October 13 with information from a report by The Times which has since been retracted, as reflected in the update on October 21.
Ever since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this past summer, the heat has been on Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president.
The whirlwind began when Infantino had proposed selling shares of the World Cup to private equity investors, which sent fans and fellow executives into a frenzy.
This scandal resulted in Infantino's position being called into question, and created a tense atmosphere in the lead-up to the upcoming FIFA presidential elections next spring.

Now, Infantino has once again been placed in the spotlight after a report — which has since been retracted — claimed he was being paid extra compensation in addition to what FIFA disclosed publicly in its 2025 annual report. That sparked a heavy response from FIFA.
MORE: Ranking the top candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or
Gianni Infantino salary as FIFA president
FIFA has committed to publishing president Gianni Infantino's salary each year in its annual report, declaring his compensation in the company's yearly release.

For the 2025 calendar year, Infantino was paid 4.8 million Swiss Francs (CHF), or $5.76 million in gross salary, according to FIFA's annual compensation report. This is broken down into 2.6 million CHF in base salary, and 2.2 million CHF in bonuses.
Report about undisclosed payment to FIFA president is retracted
According to a report by Martyn Ziegler of The Times, which has since been publicly retracted, Gianni Infantino was paid additionally on top of his disclosed salary by FIFA.

The report cites 2024 U.S. tax filings by FIFA which show that Infantino was given $1.76 million by FWC2026, the company FIFA set up to run the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States this past summer. U.S.-based non-profits must fill out IRS form 990, on which FIFA disclosed to the U.S. government payments by FWC2026 to Infantino as well as FIFA General Secretary Matias Graffstrom, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, and a number of other executives involved in the tournament's production.
This payment came on top of his regularly reported compensation, and was not publicly disclosed in FIFA's financial filings in their annual report.

However, this report was officially retracted on October 20 by The Times who conceded that FIFA's report did not disclose this additional income because Swiss tax law rules do not count expense and reimbursement payments as compensation with regards to filings and reportings by non-profits. They also acknowledged that claims regarding a Miami property purchase were false.

FIFA assert that Infantino's payments from FWC2026 were not part of his regular salary or compensation, and therefore were not required to be disclosed in their annual report by Swiss tax law, and therefore, while included in the U.S. tax filings, were not required to be publicly announced.

FIFA & FIFA PRESIDENT RECEIVES APOLOGY FROM ‘THE TIMES’ FIFA takes note of an apology published today by The Times following an inaccurate and damaging report: On 13 October 2026 (Sport), we reported that Gianni Infantino received a "second salary" from Fifa, which Fifa had failed to disclose. This is incorrect. There was no “second salary.” Regulations do not require Fifa to include expenses and reimbursements received by Mr Infantino in its annual report as they are not considered "compensation" under Swiss reporting requirements. We also accept Mr Infantino did not purchase a property in Miami at a suspected undervalue as we reported and neither he nor his family are the legal or beneficial owners of Shadi LLC and have no control over that company, as we suggested. We are happy to make these corrections and apologise to Mr Infantino and Fifa for the errors. As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA urges the media to act responsibly and carefully verify all sourcing to prevent the publication and subsequent reproduction of false and defamatory information. FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate, misleading, or totally false, as in this case, FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.
— FIFA Media (@fifamedia) October 20, 2026
Following the retraction, FIFA acknowledged the apology they received from The Times and warned there was a "concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President."

articles.headline: BioWare's cancelled Mass Effect game would've learned from Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher to deliver "a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has"
keyFacts: EA closed the BioWare studio, impacting approximately 50 staff members working on a new Mass Effect game.
BioWare veteran Tony de Waal stated the cancelled project aimed to provide unprecedented player autonomy and choice.
The development team intended to incorporate modern design techniques from the developers of Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher.
body: EA has closed its longtime studio partner BioWare, the iconic development house behind Mass Effect and Dragon Age, impacting around 50 staff who were in pre-production on the next Mass Effect game. In the aftermath of EA's decision, one of those affected has shared a little about the project, claiming it would have featured unprecedented levels of player freedom and choice reactivity.

Tony de Waal, a BioWare veteran who has worked on previous Mass Effect and Dragon Age games, offered a rare look behind the scenes at what the team was attempting. In a LinkedIn post (via PC Gamer), de Waal suggested the studio wanted to surpass the acclaimed work of the role-playing giants at Baldur's Gate 3 studio Larian and CD Projekt Red, maker of The Witcher and Cyberpunk.

"I was one of the lucky ones who stayed with BioWare to start on the next Mass Effect, where I believe we were making something special: a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match," de Waal wrote. "We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the trilogy," he added.

The veteran cinematics lead sadly didn't offer any examples of what that could've looked like in-game, but given previous Mass Effect games have incorporated a great deal of player freedom, the idea of a sequel that builds on that - while incorporating modern techniques from CDPR and Larian - would certainly have been exciting.

"I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking, and sad for the small, talented group of devs who were all punching above their weight to make something special," de Waal continued. "Please consider those who stayed with BioWare until the very end. They are truly some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career."

BioWare's closure feels sudden; it was only a year ago the studio stressed its new Mass Effect game remains in development. At the time, EA's private acquisition had just been announced. The $55bn sale has since been approved, freeing EA to start making cuts many suspected were coming.

More broadly, the move also signals an end to EA's interest in developing deep role-playing games. Outside of its sports and shooter series, EA's non-casual projects are an unannounced Star Wars Jedi sequel, and the Marvel's Iron Man game we've yet to see.

body: The 2026 NFL season is already into its seventh week, but who will be headlining the Super Bowl LXI halftime show is still yet to be announced.
However, many are speculating that Jay-Z – whose real name is Shawn Carter – will be the one to take to center stage at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles next February.
25-time Grammy Award winner Jay-Z is reportedly set to headline Super Bowl LXI halftime show Getty

Worth an estimated $2.8 billion per Forbes, the rapper is currently on the Jay-Z 30 Tour – his last full-scale tour came back in 2018 when he did the On the Run II Tour with his wife, Beyoncé – which celebrates the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt, and the 25th anniversary of The Blueprint.
To commemorate these milestones further, the release of Jay-Z in 8 – an eight-part docuseries done in conversation with producer Rick Rubin – launched last month.
Puck News were the first to report that the 25-time Grammy Award winner had allegedly chosen himself to perform on Valentines Day.

The 56-year-old is one of the co-founders of Roc Nation, an American entertainment and media company, who penned a $5 million-a-year partnership with the NFL and Apple Music to produce the halftime show.
As part of that deal, Jay-Z is the chief decision-maker and is responsible for selecting the artists who perform at the ‘Big Game’.
Per Puck’s report, though, Jay-Z appears to have picked himself over the likes of Miley Cyrus and Justin Bieber, with both having been linked to performing at SBLXI.
NFL commissioner shuts down Jay-Z rumors
But NFL commissioner Roger Goodell has very swiftly hushed those reports, insisting that a decision has not yet been made.
“I am not aware of a leak, ” Goodell said via Front Office Sports. “I’ve been in the committee meetings. So I’m not sure it’s a leak.
“We haven’t announced anything. Until we do, we won’t make any comment on that.”
Whether it’s Hov, or another artist, that will headline next year, they will have to seek to better the performance from Puerto Rican rapper Bad Bunny last year .
NFL commissioner Goodell has hushed rumors of Jay-Z being the headline act Getty
Singer Miley Cyrus is also reportedly in contention to headline in Los Angeles next February Getty
The 32-year-old made Super Bowl history by being the first Latino artist to headline solo, whilst he also became the first to deliver his performance entirely in Spanish.
Bad Bunny had Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin as guest stars, whilst there were also cameos from Pedro Pascal, Cardi B , and Karol G.

He also utilized his 15 minutes to deliver the message that “the only thing more powerful than love is hate” as a counter response to the political division and anti-immigrant rhetoric under the current U.S. President – in front of President Trump himself.
In doing so, his performance – which also included a real wedding – was hugely divisive among fans .
ESPN to broadcast Super Bowl for the first time
Looking ahead to Super Bowl LXI, it is ESPN – who paid $3 billion to acquire NFL Network back in March of this year – who will hold the broadcasting rights for the very first time.

This will see the legendary – and lengthy – partnership of Troy Aikman and Joe Buck in the booth calling their seventh Super Bowl together, although the previous six came when the pair worked for FOX.
Buck and Aikman calling Super Bowl LXI for ESPN will likely be the final chapter of their 25-year on-air partnership Getty

The occasion could well mark the very last time that they are in the broadcast booth together following reports that tension has come between the pair stemming from Buck being extended by ESPN on a six-year deal worth an estimated $108 million .
Aikman, on the other hand, will become a free agent after the 2026 season is all wrapped up.

articles.headline: "It just seemed arbitrary, and not very smart": EA was never a responsible owner for Bioware, but the developer never seemed to learn from their mistakes
keyFacts: Electronic Arts has closed the veteran RPG developer Bioware 19 years after acquiring the studio.
Former developers claim EA imposed corporate pressures while Bioware consistently struggled to define project visions early in development.
The studio faced years of staff layoffs and project cancellations before its final closure.
body: 19 years after buying Bioware, Electronic Arts have closed the veteran RPG developer. But as saddening as this is, bringing an end to series such as Dragon Age and Mass Effect, EA have never had an easy relationship with the studio.

Looking through old interviews with developers who worked across Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect, and Anthem, the corporation immediately changed the atmosphere of the studio and never seemed to understand what exactly they had bought, or even why.

However, another thread of the conversations is that from project to project, Bioware repeated the same mistakes, getting years into projects before working out what they were trying to make. Sometimes they could pull an exceptional game out of this mess, but other times it led to costly missteps like Anthem.

Back when I was running TechRadar Gaming, features editor Jeremy Peel worked with Jon Bailes to produce the oral history of Mass Effect. I'm hideously biased, but it's an excellent account of that game's development. It was during the RPG's creation that EA acquired Bioware, and developers on the game immediately noticed a change.

"What I noticed once EA came in was how the language changed at work, and started adopting more corporate-isms, like the language of corporate America," audio design lead Steve Sim recalled. "At one time if you needed help on a project, you'd say, 'I need more guys,' or 'I need more people to help me out with this.' And then it turned into, 'I need more resources.' So the biggest change I found was just the change in the language, especially amongst producers and that type of crowd. They were assimilating into the Borg, it seemed."

It's the kind of language that you will find through the open letter published by EA's chief operating officer David Tinson and chief studios officer Cam Weber. The first reference to Bioware's closure is tied up in the euphemism "Saying no to some things we're passionate about". Doing so, they say, "allows us to focus our teams and resources so we give our biggest opportunities everything they need to succeed."

Also speaking in the Mass Effect oral history, director of technology and Bioware co-founder Trent Oster describes the immediate costcutting EA enacted on taking over the studio. "When we were acquired we were all looking forward to it like, 'Yeah, we're owned by EA, they're going to give us a budget, we finally don't have to keep constraining ourselves and crushing things down and cutting corners.' And one of the first things they did was like, 'OK, based on your budgets, we need to cut across the company 10%.' And we were like, 'Oh, so we're not getting more, we're getting less.' That was a bit of the EA feeling. We call it the EA butter knife. It just seemed arbitrary, and not very smart."

The corporate cost cutting Oster describes took place nearly 20 years ago, but it continued throughout EA's ownership. Most recently, in 2023 when 50 staff were laid off to “shift [Bioware] towards a more agile and more focused studio”. Then in 2025, more staff were laid off, this time it was described as "taking [the] opportunity between full development cycles to reimagine how we work at BioWare".

It becomes particularly clear with Anthem, Bioware's launched-but-quickly-shuttered live-service game, how EA's influence manifested at the studio. Interviewed in the Summer Eternal Anthology, long-time Bioware writer David Gaider explains the design concept for the game seemed to be formed from executive demands. "The nearest I could tell, working in a corporate environment, was that it was a sifted-down list of bullet-point requirements, that no single person ever took responsibility for," Gaider explains. "It just kind of happened like that. There needs to be this project, so it was willed into existence, but nobody would say that before this project is actually kicked off, someone needs to take responsibility for the vision."

Mark Darrah echoes this in his own interview in the anthology. "Casey pitched the exact thing [EA execs] wanted to hear," he says. "Always online, live service, infinite revenue. Multiplayer." Darrah describes it as "a near-perfect pitch deck." But, he also questions whether "Bioware is the company to make a live service looter shooter."

However, while those ideas may have filtered down from EA and then been pitched back to them by Bioware leadership, it meant that work would begin on a project long before it had crystalised into a clear premise. "The idea was that they could kick the project off, and that the designer, the design department, or the creative director, particularly, would then create the vision," Gaider says. "But at that point, the project's already happening. So each time it felt like trying to catch a bronco bull who's already out and running and bucking, and you're just trying to keep up."
For that reason, Gaider claims "Anthem was doomed from the start."

Development on Anthem began in 2012, but when Gaider joined the project 18 months later, it was struggling. "The team on it was just going around in circles," Gaider says. They didn't know what they wanted." Hudson then left Bioware in 2014 and Darrah says "they basically ran with no leadership, for two, three years." In 2017 Hudson returned and Darrah was brought over from the team working on the next Dragon Age project. Over the next two years Anthem took shape before it eventually released in 2019, but, in doing so, it meant the Dragon Age team was also then left without leadership for the next two years.

"My biggest regret," Darrah says, "is I kind of feel like I should have told EA 'no' when they asked me to take over Anthem. I should have just let whatever was going to happen, happen at that point." He adds that leaving "Dragon Age running without an executive producer from 2017 to 2019 was bad. That was a huge mistake."

Darrah says he doesn't feel like he had a choice, however, because "EA was very good at making Bioware feel like things were very dire." Though, he points to the fact that Hudson's replacement as Bioware's general manager, Gary McKay, was able to delay Dragon Age: Veilguard through multiple financial years. "That tells me either he's magic, which is possible, or it was never quite as 'gun to our head' as we thought it was," Darrah says.
(Bear in mind Darrah was being interviwed ahead of Bioware's closure and he's referring to events in the past five years.)

However, while pressure from EA may have significantly impacted the development and direction of Bioware's games, it appears that the studio repeated the same mistake for decades. Gaider, Darrah, and the developers that contributed to the Mass Effect oral history, all say Bioware consistently got deep into projects without having a vision of what they were trying to build.

"When we started, Dragon Age's big premise was 'It's D&D, but it's not'," Gaider says in his Summer Eternal interview. "We'll just file the ID numbers enough to make it our own. We went through a long period of going around in circles on Dragon Age." Edwin's covered this as a push and pull between teams that thought they were making Conan, others thinking it was Lord of the Rings, and still others thinking they were making a new Diablo.

Gaider believes the only reason EA allowed Bioware to complete the original Dragon Age was because the team "were already halfway through development, and [EA] considered it sunk cost. They said, 'Well, you've got to finish this.' But it was clear that Electronic Arts considered Dragon Age, our initial vision, to be too old fashioned, too slow, and too ponderous."

Gaider says Mass Effect had the benefit of Casey Hudson, who was able to pull together a single vision for the project much sooner. Though this may be something of a grass is greener situation, because the developers on Mass Effect describe being on the game for three years before it started coming together and even then it was only because they had to prepare something for E3.

"It was the first time we pulled together playable moments in the engine that really proved to us what the game was capable of," Hudson says in the oral history. "Until you pull things together, it's all sort of theoretical, and you think you know what game you're making. But once you have that moment in time, where everything's pulled together, you know exactly what the game needs to be."

It was only after the vertical slice was completed, lead designer Preston Watamaniuk says, "that the team understood what we were building and was able to then work autonomously, without as much hands-on direction."

This approach continued through the years. In 2012 Bioware began work on Mass Effect: Andromeda. Three years into development they scrapped the plans and tech they were using to procedurally generate worlds switching to a more traditional style of RPG, making the bulk of the game in its final 18 months. In 2015 they started work on a their next Dragon Age project, which was shelved in 2017 in favour of the project that would become Veilguard, but that would then take another seven years to complete, with a live service component first adopted from Anthem and then dropped after Anthem's failure.

It looks to have still been a problem for the studio with its current Mass Effect project. First announced back in 2020, initially as part of the "N7 Day" and then followed up with a teaser trailer at The Game Awards, the new Mass Effect was still described in EA's open letter as in "early-development". Developers who worked on the cancelled game are saying they believe they were "making something special", and aimed build on what they saw coming out of Larian and CD Projekt Red, but six years is a long time to still be in early development and sounds a lot like the project could have fallen into the "going around in circles" Darrah described of Dragon Age and Anthem.

I am saddened by Bioware's closure. The team have put out incredible games over the decades, and it sounds like they were never a natural match for EA's executives or the corporation's goals. However, it also sounds like the studio have continued to face the same challenges on projects year after year without really learning how to avoid them.

Still, it would have been much better that they be allowed to spin off and become independent or be sold to another publisher who knows what the talented team can create, than to be closed down after years of staff layoffs and project cancellations.

articles.headline: Omar addresses rumors she’s related to her ex-husband: ‘Not to my knowledge’
keyFacts: Rep. Ilhan Omar dismissed rumors that she married her brother and ex-husband Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, stating "Not to my knowledge."
Federal authorities executed a search warrant on Omar's Washington, D.C., home on Oct. 12, seizing 17 items.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and other officials suggested that authorities have evidence indicating the marriage was an immigration scheme.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) waved off rumors that she married her brother , replying, “Not to my knowledge,” when asked if she was related to her ex-husband.

Omar married Ahmed Nur Said Elmi in 2009, and they divorced in 2017. The rumor that he was her biological brother, and that they married to fraudulently get him citizenship, has dogged her for years. It gained increasing credence when police raided her Washington, D.C. home on Oct. 12 under a judicially authorized warrant. In an interview with MS Now, Omar discussed the supposed origins of the claim, dismissing it as a conspiracy theory.

“It started with the Somali blog … somebody put in there that. .. he had to have been my brother or something to that effect. And right-wing conspiracy theorists in Minneapolis got a hold of it, and they just kind of went and like found random people who are like, ‘she introduced us, you know, she introduced him to us and said he was her brother,’ which is, you know, insane. I mean… I don’t know those people that they talk about,” Omar said.
When asked in a follow up question if there was any “weird kernel of truth” to the claim she was related to the man in question, Omar replied, “Not to my knowledge.”
Her response was widely mocked by conservatives online. One commenter referred to Omar as “The Mogadishu Candidate,” parodying the famous movie and novel, The Manchurian Candidate .
Despite her denials, legal experts have warned that her case is looking increasingly worrying.

“I can’t say it looks particularly great for Congresswoman Omar at this moment,” Tom Dupree, a constitutional law attorney and former deputy assistant attorney general, told NewsNation on Wednesday, after the court filing that granted the search warrant was released to the public.

Officials have reportedly obtained her DNA in connection with the case, the New York Post reported, though Omar said in the interview that nothing with her DNA was taken during the search. She said the agents “went room by room” and “took 17 items.”
DID ILHAN OMAR MARRY HER OWN BROTHER? THE CLAIMS EXPLAINED

Among the things taken in the raid were her daughter’s old cellphone, her current husband’s notebooks, a Somali phrase book, and a camera. The congresswoman said she would have to move residences in Washington, D.C., as she now feels unsafe.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin suggested last month that the agency has actionable evidence to believe that the congresswoman, a naturalized U.S. citizen since 2000, married her own brother as part of an immigration scheme. Several Trump administration officials have backed this up, including President Donald Trump, who suggested she could soon be deported.

body: - Hide.me VPN has introduced a completely redesigned dashboard for both its Android mobile and Android TV applications.
- The powerful SmartGuard feature, designed to block intrusive ads, trackers, and malicious websites, is also now available on the Android TV app.
- This update also brings stability improvements to the WireGuard and SSTP protocols, alongside new speed indicators to help pick the fastest servers.
Hide.me VPN has just rolled out a major update for its Android users, focusing on making its applications cleaner, faster, and much safer to use on the big screen.

The update introduces a completely redesigned dashboard, available across both Android mobile and Android TV. This visual overhaul makes it significantly easier to navigate your connection settings and find the optimal server for your needs with just a few taps.
But the biggest news for avid streamers is the arrival of SmartGuard on the Android TV app.

Previously limited to other platforms, SmartGuard is Hide.me's comprehensive online security tool built specifically to block intrusive ads, stop hidden trackers, and keep you away from malicious websites that can compromise your privacy.

Smart TVs and streaming boxes are notorious for tracking user behavior and monitoring what you watch to serve heavily targeted advertisements. With this update, Android TV users finally get the same robust ad-blocking power that mobile users have enjoyed. It makes it much harder for third-party snoopers and malicious actors to steal your information while you sit on the couch and stream your favorite shows.
WireGuard tweaks and IPv6 support
Hide.me has also bundled several vital technical enhancements into this release to keep your connection as stable and fast as possible.
For starters, fans of the lightning-fast WireGuard protocol will benefit from new stability enhancements and MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) optimization.

In simple terms, this ensures your data encryption remains rock-solid even if your mobile connection is unstable. If you regularly switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data networks while gaming or browsing, these tweaks will help keep your connection drop-free.

Hide.me has also improved its SSTP protocol support by adding hostname and IPv6 global address compatibility. To top it off, the update brings new speed indicators to the dashboard so you can easily identify the fastest servers at a glance, plus the addition of the Korean language to the app's supported list.

If you already have Hide.me installed on your Android smartphone, tablet, or Android TV, this update should roll out automatically depending on your device's auto-update settings.
